name: geology
title: Geology
scope: Intro geology for the rock cycle, igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rocks, plate boundaries, and mineral versus rock.
method: Decide whether the question is the rock cycle, a plate boundary, or mineral versus rock.
Define a mineral as one substance with a definite composition and an ordered atomic structure.
Define a rock as a solid aggregate, usually of one or more minerals, and not as a single mineral by default.
Place a rock in the cycle: igneous from cooled melt, sedimentary from compacted or cemented sediment, metamorphic from solid-state heat and pressure.
Name the plate tectonics boundary as divergent, convergent, or transform.
Match the motion: apart, together (a convergent subduction zone when one plate descends), or sliding past.
Compare the evidence you have, such as crystals, layers, foliation, or a Mohs hardness scratch, and say what is still missing.

formulas.name: Density
formulas.use: Density is mass divided by volume and helps compare mineral samples when both are measured.

formulas.name: Plate rate
formulas.use: An average plate rate is the distance a plate moves divided by the time that motion took.

formulas.name: Mineral vs rock
formulas.expr: mineral = one substance with an ordered structure; rock = a solid aggregate of minerals
formulas.use: Use this to keep a mineral name from being treated as a rock name.

formulas.name: Rock cycle paths
formulas.expr: melt cools to igneous; sediment compacts to sedimentary; solid-state heat and pressure make metamorphic
formulas.use: Name the path from the process, not from the color of the sample.

checks: A mineral is not the same thing as a rock; many rocks contain several minerals.
Igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic names record how the rock formed.
Divergent, convergent, and transform are three different plate-boundary motions.
Metamorphism in this card is solid-state change; melting would leave that path and can start an igneous rock.
limits: This is classification and process, not a hand-sample or site identification by itself.
It does not give mining, blasting, drilling, or extraction steps.
Plate-boundary types are general patterns, not a local map or a hazard forecast.
